publisher: NASA/JPL, distributed via the PDS Geosciences Node
title: Mars 2020 Rover PLACES (Position and Attitude Computation Engine for Surface) data localization bundle
formats_present: PDS4-labeled delimited CSV (best_interp.csv, best_tactical.csv, observations.csv, telemetry.csv, sclk_table.csv)

coordinate_reference_system.name: Jezero site-frame localization (planetocentric lat/lon + projected northing/easting)
coordinate_reference_system.datum: reported alongside radius/areoid fields per record; not independently re-derived here
coordinate_reference_system.latitude_convention: planetocentric (field: planetocentric_latitude); planetodetic latitude is also reported per-record
coordinate_reference_system.longitude_convention: east-positive (field: longitude), consistent with this project's Jezero_Crater_Projection
coordinate_reference_system.projected_fields: northing/easting in metres, described by the PDS4 label as meters north of the equator / east of the prime meridian at the projection's first standard parallel -- the same equidistant-cylindrical convention (standard parallel 18.4663N) recorded in data/metadata/spatial_reference.json for this project's DEM and zones

attribution: Mars 2020 Rover PLACES, PDS Geosciences Node, NASA/JPL-Caltech.
access_and_use_conditions: Public NASA PDS archive product; no separate license beyond standard PDS usage terms.

verification.online_verification_note: Verified from the locally bundled PDS4 XML labels and CSV data already present in the repository under data/raw/jezero/; the pds-geosciences.wustl.edu landing page was not re-fetched in this environment.
verification.internal_cross_check: The SITE 1 (sol 0) record in best_interp.csv matches the base_location() value already used by backend/app/zones.py (easting 4354494.09 / northing 1093299.70), confirming best_interp.csv and best_tactical.csv share one consistent localization and CRS.
